thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Gains 150 Points, Nasdaq Rises on a Tech Surge

author: Crystal Kim
title: Intraday Update: Dow Gains 150 Points, Nasdaq Rises on a Tech Surge
text:
By Crystal Kim July 31, 2018 1:34 p.m. ET Stay Positive. The technology-stock-loaded Nasdaq Composite has an edge over other broad market indices as investors show their optimism ahead of Apple's earnings expected after the close. If the bad news bears don't show up before then, the S&P 500 will close out July with a bang—its best showing since January. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...wonder how important Apple (AAPL) actually is to the tech sector;
•...highlight important upcoming events;
•...are revved up for engine maker Cummins (CMI) earnings.
Curb Your Optimism? Investors are breathing a sigh of relief after a rather moody Monday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average has risen nearly 170 points, or 0.7%, to 25,475.55, while the S&P 500 has risen 0.8% to 2823.70. But the Nasdaq is stealing the spotlight, rising nearly one percentage point to 7705.22.
The Nasdaq's leadership so far today is like a bandage for a gaping cut. Investors appear optimistic in anticipation of Apple earnings, but the company's results–no matter how good–may not be the saving grace for technology stocks or even the Faang stocks or Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet (GOOGL) they think it is.
Illustration: courtesy of Apple That's because Apple doesn't really move like the rest of the Faangs. After the iPhone maker reported first-quarter earnings, its stock moved sideways for the next 10 weeks. Meanwhile, the rest of the Faang stocks have seen a 20% lift, on average, Instinet technical analyst Frank Cappelleri wrote in a report. That could mean that Apple's stock is set up to see more activity, but that doesn't necessarily mean it'll move the rest of the Faangs or the entire technology complex.
In fact, because of earnings season–when stocks tend to hold hands less–Apple may dance to a different beat. The stock market's implied correlation and realized correlation are at lows, notes Jim Strugger , MKM Partners ' derivatives strategist. He explained in a report published Monday: "It can be interpreted to mean that dispersion is elevated and stocks are trading idiosyncratically on company-specific information flow. It's an environment that is typically appreciated as a boon for active investors who should be adept at capturing alpha from these single stock idiosyncrasies."
Things to keep an eye on this week: central bank meetings and wages.
Tomorrow, it's all about the Federal Reserve . There's very little chance of a rate hike this week, but what occurs in the meeting will be a sign of hikes to come. And Friday's jobs report will set the beat for stocks to dance to for the next few weeks. Leuthold Group 's Jim Paulsen sees a "wage whoosh" coming. "Pressure on labor compensation, has actually increased considerably in the last few quarters, not because the unemployment rate is low, but because economic growth has strengthened," he wrote in a note published Tuesday.
That could show up on Friday or further down the line. That's one more reason companies might have a harder time topping quarterly results. Don't forget, executives have been fixated on operating margins this earnings season and forecasts have been tracking lower compared with June levels for more than a third of S&P 500 companies. A "wage whoosh" could thin those margins out in the coming quarters.
Midday Movers BP (BP) is up 1.7% to $45.18 following its second-quarter earnings. The oil giant earned 14 cents per American depositary share on revenue of $75.44 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 14 cents per ADS on revenue of $82.25 billion. It bought back $200 million in stock in the first half of the year.
Illustration: Ed Schipul Cummins (CMI) is up 3% to $141.31 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The engine maker earned $4.14 a share on revenue of $6.13 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $3.66 a share on revenue of $5.81 billion. For the full year, it sees revenue of $23.49 billion to $23.9 billion, compared with the $23.02 billion consensus.
Johnson Controls (JCI) up 2.7% to $37.39 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The industrial conglomerate earned 81 cents a share on revenue of $8.12 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 79 cents on revenue of $7.96 billion.
Sogou (SOGO) is down 2.8% to $9.28 after Deutsche Bank downgraded the American depositary receipts of the Chinese Internet firm to Sell following lackluster quarterly results .
WisdomTree Investments (WETF) is down 2.7% to $8.88 after Citigroup downgraded it to Neutral. — Teresa Rivas
